claims.quote: Acute acetaminophen toxicity is treated with N-acetylcysteine.

claims.text: and is also recommended by professional societies for other causes of acute liver failure (evidence less definitive).
claims.quote: Administration of N-acetylcysteine is also recommended by professional societies for other causes of acute liver failure, although the supporting evidence is less definitive than for its use in acetaminophen toxicity

claims.text: Mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg (repeat once or twice as needed) temporarily lowers cerebral blood flow; contraindicated with acute kidney injury; check serum osmolality before a second dose.
claims.quote: To temporarily decrease cerebral blood flow: Mannitol (0.5 to 1 g/kg, repeated once or twice as needed) can be given to induce osmotic diuresis, and possibly brief hyperventilation can be used, particularly when herniation is suspected. (However, mannitol is contraindicated with acute kidney injury, and serum osmolality must be checked before giving a second dose.)

claims.text: Lactulose and rifaximin haven't been shown to help encephalopathy in acute liver failure.
claims.quote: There is no evidence that treatments such as lactulose or rifaximin help alleviate encephalopathy in acute liver failure
